accuracy.evidence: Rules checked against the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 2 (Year 3 introduces inverted commas, Year 4 uses them with punctuation inside, e.g. a comma after the reporting clause and end punctuation within the inverted commas: The conductor shouted, "Sit down!"), the KS2 GPS test framework glossary entry for direct speech, CCSS L.3.2c and L.4.2b, and the Oxford and Cambridge style guidance on dialogue: a statement before a following reporting clause ends with a comma, ? and ! are kept with no added comma, the reporting verb after the speech is lower case, and a leading reporting clause takes a comma with the speech opening on a capital. Every lab line and item was re-read against these rules; exclamation marks were left out of the choose-the-mark options so no option is ambiguous.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors listed in KS2 writing moderation exemplars and teacher guidance for Year 3 and 4: punctuation outside the closing mark (step 2 prediction, challenge 'outside', m1), speech marks round the whole sentence including the reporting clause (step 1 prediction, challenge 'all'), full stop before said (step 3, step 4 Raj line, challenge 'stop', m9), capital Asked or Said after the speech (step 4 Lily line, challenge 'cap', m4), lower-case start after Mum said (step 4, challenge 'low', p4), missing comma after said (challenge 'nocomma'), comma added after a question mark (challenge 'both', m3) and speech marks on reported speech (step 5, challenge 'rep', p5, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdspeech works on the mechanics of a single line of direct speech: a comic face and bubble whose words must be found inside the sentence, a row of empty gap slots where the opening and closing marks are placed in turn, a box inside the closing mark filled from comma, full stop or question mark, a one-slip hunt, and a direct versus reported sort. flagdlg (ages 11-14) is dialogue craft (new speaker new paragraph, action beats, voice, endings), flagquote quotes from texts, flagcomma is commas in lists. Gate similarity is under 30% to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule by acting: tapping shouted or the speaker's name is refused because it is not in the bubble; a closing mark placed before the comma is refused with the reason the comma belongs to the speech; a full stop before said Mum is refused because the sentence goes on; the capital Asked is the slip to find; and the reported cards are refused from the speech-marks box because they are not exact words. Each completion message states the rule just found.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'I am cold, said Sam' inside the marks (the bubble step shows only the spoken words go in), 'Before the comma: here”,' (the gap step refuses that gap), and 'Yes, Tom is talking' for Tom said that he was cold (the sort refuses it as not his exact words).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages from why(): comma outside, marks round the reporting clause, full stop before said, capital Said, reported speech in marks, small letter to start the speech, missing comma after said, name versus exact words, loud versus spoken, comma after a question mark, and the question mark outside the closing mark. The lab steps give a reason for every wrong tap as well.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads well under the family limit of grade 5.0 (measured 0.1 by learn/readability.py fk_grade), adult at 9.2 (limit 10.0). Kid sentences are short and concrete (The name and said stay outside the marks.). Canvas labels are short: 'Line 1 of 3: tap the words Tom says', 'Found 1 of 2 spoken words', 'which mark goes in the box?'. Adult text names direct speech, reported speech, inverted commas, reporting clause and the US term quotation marks.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one rule: marks round exact words, name and said outside, the mark inside and comma before said, speaker first, reported speech. Items spread across finding spoken words (p1, m8), counting marks and bubbles (p2, m5), the mark inside (p3, m7), speaker-first lines (p4), reported speech (p5, m6) and spotting the slip (m1, m3, m4, m9) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 x 640 Android screenshots in light and dark at the start, during Show me and at the end of every step: sentence tokens wrap onto two or three centred rows with nothing clipped, the gap slots stay at least 24 px wide, the three mark buttons fit side by side at about 96 px each with their names, the sort bin titles shrink to fit their box after a fix, and the challenge banner was shortened after it clipped at 360 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin below the canvas: one button per word in the bubble step, one per gap labelled 'Mark between here and ,' or 'Mark at the very end', one per mark with its name (', comma'), one per part of the slip line labelled 'Is the closing mark wrong?' for the speech marks, and the two sort boxes. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the result and the reason. walk.cjs ran every task with Show me and axe WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console or page errors.
